title: Practical Federated Recommendation Model Learning Using ORAM with Controlled Privacy
problem: Federated learning (FL) for recommendation models is impractical because the large embedding tables require each user to access a tiny fraction of table entries, and hiding those access patterns via ORAM incurs prohibitive latency and SSD wear. Existing ORAM-based approaches have latency and SSD lifetime overheads that make them undeployable at scale.
motivation: Recommendation models hold commercially sensitive embedding tables that cannot be centralized, but FL is blocked by the massive table sizes and the need to obliviously access them, making privacy-preserving training practically infeasible today.
method: FEDORA places the large ORAM structure on SSDs rather than DRAM, using SSD-friendly access optimizations to reduce write amplification and wear. It introduces epsilon-FDP (Federated Differential Privacy), a formal framework that trades off ORAM privacy strength against performance by allowing a controlled, quantified privacy budget, reducing the number of ORAM operations required. The system also supports modern FL operation modes (e.g., asynchronous and partial participation) so it integrates with production FL pipelines.
key_novelty: Epsilon-FDP is a new formal privacy notion that explicitly balances ORAM obliviousness against performance cost, enabling practical SSD-backed ORAM for federated recommendation training.
contributions: epsilon-FDP: a formal privacy-performance tradeoff framework for ORAM in federated settings
SSD-backed ORAM placement with SSD-friendly access pattern optimizations
Support for modern FL operation modes (asynchronous, partial participation)
Up to 24x latency reduction and over 1000x SSD lifetime improvement over ORAM baseline

metrics.speedup: up to 24x latency reduction; 5x average latency improvement over baseline
metrics.other: over 1000x SSD lifetime improvement (peak); 158x average SSD lifetime improvement

limitations: The epsilon-FDP privacy guarantee is weaker than full ORAM obliviousness; quantifying acceptable privacy loss for production deployments requires careful per-deployment analysis.
primary_theme: ORAM-backed federated learning for recommendation models
